bead.title: SQLite terminal reap sweep
bead.description: PROBLEM: the sqlite relational backend reclaims leases and cohorts but does not sweep terminal rows with the required retention-and-cursor conjunction, so opt-in terminal records never age out. ROOT CAUSE: `crates/pqueue-sqlite/src/relational.rs:8063-8166` implements `ReclaimDriver::tick` for lease and cohort expiry only; the terminal reap predicate already exists in `crates/pqueue-sqlite/src/relational.rs:2206-2265` but is not invoked from the tick path. PROPOSED FIX: wire the sqlite tick path to the terminal sweep using the durable emission cursor from `pqueue-657e5f8d`, reaping terminal rows only when retention has elapsed and the cursor has passed for emit-enabled queues, while preserving retention-only behavior for opt-out queues. NON-SCOPE: do not change Postgres, the composed backend tick wiring, metrics export, evidence ledger, or unrelated lease/cohort reclamation semantics; dependency `pqueue-509a70d0` stays intact.
bead.acceptance: 1. `TestSqliteTerminalReapSweepsWithCursorConjunction` covers emit-enabled queues and proves terminal rows are reaped only after both retention and cursor conditions are satisfied. 2. `TestTerminalReapOptOutIgnoresCursor` covers opt-out queues and proves terminal rows reap on retention alone. 3. `go test ./...` passes. 4. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
